comparator.name: Cybersecurity & Cybercrime
comparator.sourceNotes: Fresh current2026–2027 official guide confirms a Dutch three-year180-EC programme starting in September2025, with cybersecurity governance, computing, law and criminology integrated through skills/research and project work. Eleven compulsory units in each of years1 and2 independently total60+60=120 EC. The current programme overview separately and explicitly reserves30 EC of genuine free-choice space in year3: individual courses, a minor, study abroad or a relevant internship, with internship content arranged with the study coordinator. This real30-EC space is preserved as one component, without invented course content, bringing the supported partial reconstruction to150 EC. The guide still states that third-year course records become visible from June2027 and lists no third-year modules. The overview describes a10-EC integration course in each year but does not identify the third-year unit, complete compulsory later-year membership or final assessment conditions; it cannot supply a complete remaining30-EC core. The overview disciplinary allocations are aggregate thematic descriptions, not additional courses to add to the existing120. Neither those blocks nor a speculative thesis, project, fourth-year component or elective filler is appended. The remaining30 EC of compulsory year3 requirements, exact project/final assessment and formal progression/choice conditions remain unestablished. No formal route or UCR assessment is introduced. This is a finite first-stage correction; remaining external questions do not authorise recurring evidence monitoring.
